ratings.comment: Very passionate about Southeast Asia. Essay exams based on the readings, but it's not necessary to actually read them; can just pull quotes when writing the essays. Comprehensive lecture slides that lay out the whole picture. Fun guy!

He's probably my favorite professor I've had thus far. You must attend the lecture and take notes because he goes through a lot of information, but it's interesting. He's eccentric: makes a lot of jokes, talks about movies, and gets off topic. In the honors section, he leads the discussion, but he just answers your questions. Take this class!

Dr Mike is great and passionate. Layout of class is tough, SO many readings and harsh essays. Essays had absolutely no clear criteria or rubric and I would get downgraded for the smallest things, and I had to pry for an explanation. Don't take for an "easy" ethnic studies credit, much better options available. Only plus is zero tests

Interesting course content, especially in the readings/memoirs. Rubric requirements not clear for honors section. Grading system not clear. When I asked what an A was for the class he did not have a numerical answer. It seems that grades are decided based on first impressions rather than actual work. Maybe those who had TA had different experiences

His lectures are very long, but is VERY knowledgeable about SE Asia. This class was interesting and you do not necessarily have to read everything he gives you to do well. If you are remotely interested in the subject, take it. Just show up to lecture and go to discussion and you'll do great.

Cullinane was funny sometimes, but I've never met anyone who went through content as simultaneously quickly and slowly as he does. The readings were repetitive and boring. He does offer extra credit for people who know more than what's expected, though. Still, I get why people like him and his classes - he's a good guy with good one-liners.

Lectures are impossibly dense and long, assigns an unmanageable amount of readings and films, two intense papers due within a week of each other at the end of the semester. Does not grade with a rubric (just how he feels).

Professor Cullinane knows what he's talking about, but his lectures are super long. I have to watch them on 2x speed in order to make it through them without falling asleep. I learned a lot in his class and would recommend it if you're interested, but if you just need a requirement and don't really care about SE Asia, definitely skip it.

Interesting class about Southeast Asia. I waited to long to actually read the books for the fiction project so that stressed me out a little. He's a very good lecturer and encourages students to come and talk to him outside of class. I didn't bother reading most of the articles assigned, as long as you attend class and take notes you're good.

Not an intriguing class if you have no interest in Southeast Asia. I definitely learned a lot, despite being bored (through very long lectures). Very knowledgeable professor. You only have to write two papers -- a take-home midterm essay and a writing project. The final is an in-class essay and worth 40% of your grade, use your note sheet well!

Even though I hated the class I took, I absolutely loved Professor Cullinane. I am not a huge history buff but he made it as enjoyable as it could have been with his witty comments and quirky tangents. He also always does review sessions which are an incredible help and it is clear that he wants his students to do well.

Professor Cullinane is an awesome professor. His lectures can get long and he uses no visual aids for lecture, but if you go and take notes it is an easy A. I didn't go to class hardly at all and got the notes from a friend (although I would not advise doing this). Would recommend. DISCUSSION IS MANDATORY.

Cullinane is a very interesting character. He is very knowledgeable about the countries of Southeast Asia. He is a head person at the Center for Southeast Asian Studies in Madison. I learned a lot in this course but the expected time outside of class was pretty ridiculous. Over the course I read a book, 47 articles, and watched 9 docs (all required

He makes the material a lot more interesting that it usually would be, and it's especially helpful that he was so loud as well as added funny commentary to get through the hour and a half long lecture.

This man is amazing! He really knows his stuff, and he's passionate about it, which makes the whole thing less boring than it should be. You may get sleepy, because he talks for an hour and a half, but he'll give you a detailed outline of what we're seeing, including key terms. Expect weekly readings, although his exams are not that tough.

He's like, 80 and hilarious. He'll just stand and talk at you for an hour and half, no power point, so make sure to pay attention in lecture. He has a bad habit of using too many pronouns, so if you zone out for a min you'll come back to a lecture full of "and then they" ,"they did" , etc and you'll never know who "they" are. Overall like the class

Great historian, really makes the history come alive and has fun doing it. He has a movie reference for everything and is very easy to talk to and ask for help or clarification. Doesn't bombard you with work and tries his best to make it easy on you. Take it for honors credit, he teaches the honors discussion and it's easier than the standard.

His roller coaster voice will ceaselessly shift from whisper to shout during his lectures. His endless movie references will make you question whether you have taken a cinematography lecture. His shady FBI history will make you skeptical of his past. All that means is AWESOME prof. Take him. Hail to the chief! Salutes to General Patrick Swayze!

Awesome professor! He is really excited and passionate about teaching the subject. Lectures were very stimulating and I didn't mind that it was a power lecture. The class overall is easy and your grade is based on the TA.

Really awesome lecturer - he will keep you awake even during an early morning power lecture! Class is very interesting but fast paced. If you go to lecture and pick up on the main themes, you'll do fine. Tests are extremely simple and straightforward. Review sessions clear up any confusion. An A is definitely possible with a little effort.

Good guy, interested in the subject and extremely knowledgable.  Helpful outside of class.  Lecture was unorganized, no visual aids or books other than his outlines. Power lecture was painful to sit through, 75 minutes of his random ranting.  Class wasn't difficult, but wouldn't recommend it.  Grade entirely dependent on TA.
Really cool dude. Class is designed to be about what you absorbed, not what you memorize. Overall very interesting and his lectures are informative and hilarious.

A very dynamic lecturer, and a nice guy as well. His lectures are vital for success in his class. He allows students a lot of flexibility in this class, letting them focus on areas that interest them. I'd definitely take him again.
Great prof, really knows what he's talking about. A lot of reading though, and you have to attend lecture. Speaks fast, lectures can be a bit boring but you'll be able to get through it.

Lots of reading.  Speaks very fast during lecture and there is no powerpoint or notes.  But he is hilarious and a great guy.  Very passionate about what he's teaching.  Don't expect an easy A, but it's not too hard.

Really LOVES what he teaches! Speaks incredibly fast so be prepared to take good, quick notes. Lecture is not mandatory, but if you don't go you will fail (no online notes or anything). He goes through material quickly; there is a TON of reading. Midterm was a breeze, but be sure to have a good notecard for the final.

He's a great guy, to be sure, but this class is so unstructured that it's frustrating! Discussions have no relations to lecture, it's frustrating that there doesn't seem to be a rubric for exams that he grades in ways that he likes instead of what you argue. Talk to him in his office hours though and he'll help you out a lot.
Great Prof, very interested in the topic and shows enthusiasm when teaching. Grade based on disc grade, book assignment(2 books), midterm, and final. Learned a lot and enjoyed the class. Take him!

Really good class, learn a lot about Vietnam, The Philippines, Thailand, and Indonesia.  Cheat sheet on final exam so make sure to actually go to lecture and take decent notes.  Overall great professor

This professor was the man! I'm not a history major but I really enjoyed the class. It might seem difficult in the beginning but it gets a lot easier after the midterm. Take good notes because they'll help you out big time...especially for the open note final

AWESOME professor. Loves this subject and makes lectures interesting. He is always available if you need help and will work around your schedule. I had him for discussion in honors section and he'll help you with any questions you have. Also, the tests are only on what he says is on the test. No tricks or games. Great class, great professor!
Professor Cullinane is my hero.  You can't ask for a better prof.  Seriously.

Great class. Lectures are informative and as interesting as a power lecture can be.  The class is easy, with an emphasis on writing with a paper as a midterm, a paper on two books, and a blue book final.  Readings not bad.
Fun, lively guy... makes it easy to do a 9:30 class. Tells the history of a spoonful of sugar and the King and I. open note final
Great professor and a very engaging lecturer.  I'd definitely recommend taking this class-just pray Ruth de Llobet isn't your TA!!

Fantastic professor.  Very funny and excited about the subject, and thrilled to teach you about anything related to SE Asia.  I did very few of the readings, went to every class, and got an A.  Honors section is interesting and fun too.
Easy course.  You don't even have to do the reading as long as you pay attention in lecture and know what each reading is about.  Lectures are pretty good as well.
No Comments
This guy is great, he reminds me of Harry Carey.  He's got a good sense of humor and makes tuesday morning class lots of fun.
Fun, exciting lecture.  Never a dull moment.
Very exciting and dynamic.  Always willing to help students.  Tells you exactly what will be on the final exam ;).
